# Epic 4 original reference input

Status: story 4.1 validated original fixture baseline. Product integration, ECU delivery and complete SC1 acceptance remain downstream gates.

The positive ARXML files are product-original descriptions for `epic4-win64-sr-cs-v1`. They preserve separate file boundaries, including `unrelated.arxml`. The external R24-11 XSD and ECUC MOD archives remain under the ignored official-document directory; they must not be copied into a reference package. External definition references are resolved against the pinned local MOD archive.

`types.arxml` describes the uint32 application/implementation mapping and the four-byte diagnostic OUT array. `application.arxml` has one application instance, explicit receive/send points, a 10 ms TimingEvent and the same component's synchronous server. `services.arxml` declares the Dcm service client; its target-side implementation is a future story 4.13 producer, not an existing exported C function. `extract.arxml` connects system signals, I-Signals, PDUs, frames, triggerings, communication ports and the target ECU. `ecuc.arxml` carries the selected OS/RTE/communication/diagnostic values. `bsw.arxml` identifies current host implementation entries and their actual periodic entities; these host entry names do not claim complete standardized BSW APIs.

R24-11 MOD module revisions are `4.10.0` (read from their DOC-REVISION), separately from the release name and `AUTOSAR_00053.xsd` schema identifier. `DcmDspDataByteSize=4` expresses the contract's 32-bit diagnostic element using the actual R24-11 parameter. Its OPAQUE representation prevents Dcm from exchanging the server's already big-endian bytes.

Additional diagnostic reference settings use 64-byte transport buffers, N_As/N_Bs/N_Cr = 200 ms, P2 = 50 ms, P2* = 5000 ms. These are declared reference configuration choices; 4.2 must bind their normative conditions and independent response expectations before dependent generators are accepted. Physical normal addressing, padding to DLC 8, and read-only DID 0x1234 remain the fixed integration contract. S3 is a normative timeout, not an invented ECUC parameter. No new OS, RTE or diagnostic implementation is claimed by these fixtures.

The original BSW description currently covers the selected current host interfaces. Full module obligations, native hardware-only configuration applicability, generated adapters, service linkage and C-artifact quality remain explicit downstream obligations. A schema pass alone cannot establish those gates.

The 17 current BSW entries contain their actual return/argument descriptions. The `Host_*` base types bind existing C header declarations at the fixed x64 ABI; pointer declarations preserve pointer direction, and C array parameters use their adjusted pointer signature. These are host implementation types, separate from the application's uint32 mapping. The independent auditor checks both ARXML signatures and the real header/implementation declarations. Initialization entries use UNSPECIFIED execution context because StartupHook initialization is not Task context. Periodic entities require SCHEDULED/TASK as required by BSW Module Description Template `constr_4017`; the Com transmit entity is explicitly mapped after the application and before Dcm.
